 Voting in North Carolina? Make a Plan
 Voting in North Carolina? Make a Plan 
 October 26, 2026
 Contact 
 Lauren Reese 
 As the upcoming midterm election approaches, Davidson College encourages all eligible students to make a plan to cast their ballots. Whether voting locally in Mecklenburg County or via absentee ballot in another state, campus resources are available to guide students through every step of the process. 
 Pushpin 
 Key Takeaways
 Where can I vote early? Cornelius Town Hall 
 When does early voting in NC end? Saturday, Oct. 31 
 Do I need to bring an ID to vote in person? Yes. 
 If I am using my CatCard for ID, can I use the mobile version? No. You have to have a physical CatCard. You can get a physical CatCard in Alvarez College Union. 
 Can I register to vote on Election Day? No. You can only register to vote during the early voting period. 
 When is Election Day? Tuesday, Nov. 3 
 Will transportation to the polls be available for students on Nov. 3? Yes. See WildcatSync for details. 
 Dates and Locations
 Early Voting in North Carolina: The last day to vote early in North Carolina is Saturday, Oct. 31. The closest early voting site to campus is Cornelius Town Hall, 21445 Catawba Ave, Cornelius, NC. North Carolina allows same-day voter registration during the early voting window with acceptable proof of residency.  
 Election Day: Tuesday, Nov. 3 is the final day to vote in the midterm elections. Davidson students who registered using their Davidson College campus address must cast their ballots at their assigned precinct polling location, Davidson Town Hall, 251 South St., Davidson, NC. 
 What to Bring
 North Carolina voters will be asked to show photo ID at the polls. Approved options include a valid North Carolina driver’s license, a U.S. passport, or an approved college photo ID. 
 Davidson College students may use their CatCard as an approved voter photo ID. A physical CatCard is required to vote in-person on election day. Students may obtain a physical CatCard in the Alvarez College Union. 
 Campus Resources and Guidance
 The Mulliss Center for Civic Engagement provides non-partisan voting resources for all Davidson College students:  
 Visit the  Engaging in Democracy webpage for more information regarding voting requirements in North Carolina and other states. 
 Check out the  Engaging in Democracy WildcatSync article for more information on upcoming voter education events, transportation to the polls and information regarding registering to vote in North Carolina during the early voting period.
